articles.title: Alcaraz escapa de la trampa de Arnaldi para repetir en los cuartos de Tokio
articles.standfirst: El murciano levanta cuatro pelotas de primer set (6-2 en el 'tie break') y se las verá con Shapovalov
articles.summary: El murciano levanta cuatro pelotas de primer set (6-2 en el 'tie break') ante Arnaldi y se las verá con Shapovalov
articles.body: Denis Shapovalov, uno de los 14 zurdos del 'top100', será este domingo el rival de Carlos Alcaraz en la antepenúltima ronda del Open 500 de Tokio. El murciano volvió a firmar otra remontada para ganarse el billete entre los ocho mejores. Después de sufrir con Alex Michelsen, que le obligó a disputar una manga de desempate, Alcaraz tiró de jerarquía para cerrar por la vía rápida ante Matteo Arnaldi, por 7-6(6) y 6-1, en 1 hora y 45 minutos. Por segundo día seguido se quedó a un juego del 23º rosco de su carrera. Arnaldi, semifinalista este año en Roland Garros, dispuso de un 6-2 en la muerte súbita del primer set. Fue perdiendo punto a punto, hasta seis seguidos que le darían el parcial a su condecorado verdugo. Puro ejercicio de escapismo. "Cuando te ves 6-2 abajo en el tie-break, piensas que tienes que hacer algo diferente en el segundo set, intentar mejorar y, evidentemente, ganarlo para llevarte el partido en tres sets. Simplemente intenté mantenerme ahí, punto a punto", reflexionaba el vencedor a la conclusión. El campeón de siete grandes, aliviado por haber salvado una situación de máxima presión, se desató después. No le ayudan las condiciones de la capital japonesa, con una humedad y unas pelotas que nada tienen que ver con las del O2 de Londres donde ganó la Laver Cup por Europa. Los rivales italianos le sientan bien al pupilo de Samuel López, que sólo pierde con Jannik Sinner. Así lo reflejan los últimos 26 cara a cara contra adversarios de ese país: 23 victorias y tres derrotas, todas ellas con el número 1 mundial. Este sigue sin despejar la duda de si acudirá finalmente al Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18). Carlitos se mantiene invicto en Tokio, con un 8-0. A sus 23 años, suma 59 presencias en los cuartos de torneos de categoría 500. A Shapovalov le ha ganado los dos precedentes. Por el mismo cuadrante sigue avanzando Jaume Munar, con el que podría cruzarse en semifinales. El mallorquín se las verá con el 'special exempt', Kyrian Jacquet. El triunfo de Alcaraz ante Arnaldi le permite distanciarse un poco más de Ben Shelton, que persigue un lugar en el podio mundial. La renta del español sobre el estadounidense es de 480 puntos. Shapovalov, siguiente oponente del primer cabeza de serie del cuadro nipón, es uno de los 14 zurdos del 'top100' mundial. La lista la componen Shelton (4), Learner Tien (15), Alejandro Tabilo (31), Ugo Humbert (32), Cameron Norrie (40), Shapovalov (46), Juan manuel cerúndolo (53), Facundo Díaz (69), Corentin Moutet (70), Adrian Mannarino (81), Hugo Gaston (87), Mattia Bellucci (91), Alex Molcan (96) y Terence Atmane (99).

articles.summary: El murciano se ha impuesto en los dos precedentes entre ambos
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz avanza con paso firme en Tokio y ya está a tres victorias de revalidar el título tras vencer este sábado a Matteo Arnaldi. En los cuartos del domingo le espera Denis Shapovalov, el 46 del ranking a sus 27 años. El talentoso zurdo necesitó tres sets para imponerse en la segunda ronda a Alejandro Tabilo. Alcaraz y Shapovalov se han cruzado en dos ocasiones y en ambos casos el triunfo cayó del lado del fenómeno de El Palmar. La primera vez fue en la tercera ronda de Roland Garros, en 2023, y la segunda, en la tercera ronda de Indian Wells. El canadiense, sin embargo, guarda buenos recuerdos de Tokio. Fue allí donde en 2018 logró meterse por primera vez entre los ocho mejores en un torneo de categoría 500. Hoy ha sumado la presencia 50º en los cuartos de un 50. El partido de cuartos de final de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Denis Shapovalov se disputará este domingo 4 de octubre en la central del Ariake Coliseum, en el segundo turno de la sesión diurna, sobre las 06.00 de la madrugada en España. En el primer turno saltará a jugar Jaume Munar con Kyrian Jacquet. El partido de cuartos del Open 500 de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Denis Shapovalov se podrá seguir en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Badosa cae con Ostapenko y no defiende la tercera ronda de Pekín

articles.summary: La tenista de Begur se despide tras desperdiciar un 5-3 en los dos sets
articles.body: Paula Badosa, que salvó la primera ronda del WTA 1000 de Pekín a pesar de perder ocho veces su servicio ante Daria Kasatkina, no pudo este sábado con Jelena Ostapenko, la vigésimo cuarta cabeza de serie del cuadro y que la venció por 7-6(5) y 7-5. La derrota supone que Badosa no defiende la tercera ronda de la pasada edición por lo que no mejorará su actual ranking, en el puesto 59. A pesar de estar lejos de su mejor nivel, la tenista de Begur dispuso de un 5-3 en las dos mangas. Ostapenko encadenó entonces cuatro juegos seguidos ante una rival que volvió a ceder su saque en cinco ocasiones. A Paula no le gusta jugar contra adversarias que le pegan igual o más fuerte que ella y la sacan de posiciones cómodas para golpear. Ostapenko responde a ese perfil. No es casualidad que haya decantado a su favor los últimos tres cara a cara. La pupila de Pol Toledo no supo aprovechar las 10 dobles faltas de la letona.

articles.title: Crece la incertidumbre con Sinner: se borra también de Shanghái y deja el número 1 en manos de Zverev
articles.standfirst: El italiano no juega un partido desde la final de Wimbledon por la rodilla derecha
articles.summary: El italiano no juega un partido desde la final de Wimbledon por la rodilla derecha
articles.body: Jannik Sinner sigue sin arrancar por culpa de su lesión en la rodilla derecha y las especulaciones sobre su paso por el quirófano o que ponga fin a la temporada son cada vez más fuertes. El italiano, que no disputa un partido desde la final de Wimbledon el pasado 12 de julio, se ha borrado este sábado del Masters 1000 de Shanghái. Antes lo había hecho de los TMS de Montreal y Cincinnati, del US Open y del Open 500 de Pekín. "Desafortunadamente, no voy a estar en condiciones de jugar el torneo de Shanghái", anunciaba en sus redes sociales. Su ausencia se alarga hasta los 98 días (contando la fecha final de Shanghái) y es ya más prolongada que los tres meses que tuvo que estar parado por su positivo de clostebol en Indian Wells 2024. La baja de Sinner deja el cetro de la ATP en manos de Alexander Zverev. Si el alemán conquista el título en Pekín y repite en Shanghái se convertirá en el nuevo número 1 mundial el próximo lunes 19 de octubre. Jannik, que esta semana ya ha perdido los 500 puntos al no defender la corona de Pekín, restará 50 más por la tercera ronda del Masters 1000 chino. Su sustituto en el cuadro será el australiano Hijikata. Sólo es cuestión de tiempo que Zverev se convierta en el trigésimo líder del ranking. Y es que al italiano le queda todavía por defender 3.000 puntos más porque es el vigente campeón de Viena (500), París (1000) y las ATP Finals de Turín (1.500). En el caso de Sascha son sólo 980 puntos los que debe afrontar respecto a 2025. Al campeón de cinco grandes se le vio el viernes pasando consulta en una clínica de Lyon donde fue visitado por un doctor especializado en rodillas. En sus intentos por volver a los entrenamientos en Montecarlo, tenía que retirarse de las prácticas a los 10 minutos. En el calendario de Sinner aparece como siguiente torneo el Six Kings Slam de Riad (21 al 24 de octubre) donde el transalpino empezaría en los cuartos contra Alex de Miñaur. Cabe recordar que Carlos Alcaraz y Novak Djokovic pasan directamente a las semifinales al ser lo que más títulos de Grand Slam tienen en su palmarés. El jugador de San Cándido, de 25 años, se llevó las dos primeras ediciones que le supusieron un botín de más de 10 millones de euros. Alcaraz y Sinner no coinciden en un cuadro desde el TMS de Montecarlo a principios del mes de abril. De hecho, disputaron la final, con triunfo del segundo. La posible baja del italiano para lo que resta de temporada tendría ahora mismo a Rafa Jódar como gran beneficiado. El madrileño, a pesar de encadenar primeras rondas en el US Open y Tokio, es noveno en la Race 2026, que da billete a la cita de maestros reservada a los ocho mejores. Hoy estaría en el cartel de los titulares en Turín. Jannik se aleja definitivamente de la convocatoria del equipo italiano de la Copa Davis para las finales de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre). Y es que Filippo Volandri tiene que dar la lista el próximo 26 de octubre.

articles.title: Emma Raducanu Is Going to Drop Outside The Top 100 And Yet Her Ranking Tells the Wrong Story
articles.summary: I have been pretty harsh on Emma Raducanu over the years. Some of it, I still think, was more than justified. After all, I was hardly the only voice criticiz...
articles.body:
I have been pretty harsh on Emma Raducanu over the years . Some of it, I still think, was more than justified . After all, I was hardly the only voice criticizing her choices. The coaching turnover became ridiculous at times. Some scheduling decisions were impossible to understand. Too often a promising run would be followed by another absence or another reset or another explanation for why the momentum had disappeared.

Five years after winning the US Open, that remains her only professional singles title. There has also occasionally been a tendency around Raducanu to treat perfectly normal progress as evidence that another New York miracle might be just around the corner. It usually wasn't.

Yet looking at where her career stands right now, with Raducanu sitting at No. 100 and likely to fall outside the Top 100 once more, I find it difficult to summon much criticism. This time, at least, the ranking is telling a fairly cruel story. Because Raducanu wasn't playing badly when everything stopped, she was finally playing quite well.

Raducanu's Ranking Tells the Wrong Story

This Was Supposed to Be the Year Things Settled Down

Earlier this season, Raducanu's career seemed to be moving in a direction that looked almost boring. And that's a compliment. She finished 2025 at No. 29 after completing 50 matches for the first time in her career. She entered 2026 with an established ranking, climbed as high as No. 23, and began putting together fairly ordinary results that had been strangely absent from much of her post-US Open career.

She made the final in Cluj-Napoca in February. It was her first WTA Tour final since winning the US Open in 2021 . The final itself was awful, with Cirstea beating her 6-0, 6-2, but getting there mattered. She had finally strung together four victories at one tournament again and survived an almost three-hour semi-final along the way.

Then came Queen's. That week was probably the clearest evidence that Raducanu was beginning to resemble a high-level tour player rather than somebody perpetually trying to rediscover a version of herself from five years earlier. She beat Anna Blinkova 6-0 6-3, Cirstea 6-4 6-2, Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3 7-5 and No. 19 Iva Jovic 6-2 6-2 before losing the final to Donna Vekic 6-0 7-6(6). The run lifted her to No. 31, putting her comfortably inside Grand Slam seeding territory.

Yes, there were flaws; there always are. It was still only an 11-10 record for the season after Queen's. So she had not suddenly transformed into a title machine, and another heavy final defeat raised legitimate questions about how well she was handling the physical and emotional demands of consecutive matches deep into tournaments. But something resembling a foundation remained. And as per cue, her leg broke down.

What had initially been treated as a lower-leg problem developed into a stress fracture. Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament after medical advice told her to stop playing through it. She was supposed to be the No. 30 seed. Instead, she did not play at all. And that's kind of it. She hasn't played a competitive match since the Queen's final on June 14.

Wimbledon disappeared. So did the entire North American hard-court swing. So did the US Open, the tournament around which her career will probably always orbit whether she likes it or not. And now Beijing has gone too. The ranking has responded exactly as rankings do.

No sympathy. Raducanu was No. 31 after Queen's. She fell to No. 49 in July, No. 59 in August, No. 70 after the US Open, No. 89 in September, and is now No. 100. More points are due to disappear because she cannot defend last year's China Open result. As things stand, she is likely to leave the Top 100. That looks like regression. In reality, she has barely had the opportunity to regress at all.

Sympathy should not require rewriting Raducanu's career. There are reasons she reached this point with so little protection against another long injury absence. The coaching situation is one of them. By early 2026, Raducanu had already gone through an extraordinary number of different arrangements. Francisco Roig left after the Australian Open, with the pair disagreeing over how she should play.

She later reunited with Andrew Richardson, the coach who had been alongside her during the 2021 US Open run. There have been explanations for individual changes. Nick Cavaday left for health reasons. Some partnerships were trials rather than intended long-term arrangements. It would be lazy to treat every split as Raducanu recklessly firing another coach.

The overall instability has still been real. Players build careers through repetition: same voices, same routines, same technical ideas, same preparation. Raducanu has spent significant portions of her early twenties rebuilding those habits. Her scheduling has sometimes invited criticism too. There have been stretches where she played too little to establish rhythm, and others where physical problems made every decision feel temporary.

Most importantly, availability remains part of professional sport. Unfortunately, Raducanu has repeatedly been injured, but at some point the inability to stay healthy becomes part of the career assessment itself. Her 2023 season effectively ended after Stuttgart, before surgeries on both wrists and an ankle. She fought her way back through 2024.

Then she finally managed a much fuller 2025 season, and just as 2026 appeared to be developing into something stable, another serious physical problem arrived. That doesn't happen in a vacuum. Yes, there is bad luck, but some of it wasn't due to bad luck. It's as simple as that, and it cannot be ignored. Neither can the enormous gap between what happened in New York and everything since.

Raducanu won a Grand Slam at 18. She has still never won another title. She has reached only one Grand Slam fourth round since that US Open run, at Wimbledon in 2024. The WTA's own records show only one WTA 1000 quarter-final in her career so far. Those numbers are hugely disappointing for somebody who once produced one of the most astonishing tournament runs tennis has seen.

They are also perhaps why judging Raducanu has always been so difficult. What exactly was everyone supposed to expect after 2021? It's impossible to say, because Raducanu didn't gradually become a good professional tennis player and then win something enormous. She skipped the gradual part.

She arrived at Wimbledon ranked outside the Top 300, reached the fourth round, qualified for the US Open, and won ten consecutive matches without dropping a set. The public met the finished miracle before the player had experienced most of the ordinary stages required to build a career. Everything afterward was judged backward from that.

A quarter-final looked disappointing because she had already won a major. No. 30 looked disappointing because she had already been No. 10. A first-round loss looked like evidence that New York had been some enormous accident rather than what it usually is for a young player: a first-round loss.

The US Open trophy gave Raducanu financial security, fame, and opportunities that most players could never imagine. It also created an impossible reference point.

The Ranking Drop Is the Least Interesting Part

This is where I have become more sympathetic. Raducanu is only 23. That sounds obvious, but her career has been discussed for so long that she sometimes feels considerably older. She is younger than plenty of players who are still described as developing.

Her professional tennis education has also been bizarrely fragmented. One season brought instant global fame. Another brought surgeries. Another one was spent reconstructing a ranking. Just as she finally completed a relatively normal 50-match year, another significant injury removed several months.

Yet when she has actually been able to play for sustained periods, there have been signs of progress. She finished 2024 at No. 58. She finished 2025 at No. 29. She reached No. 23 this year. She's also made finals, so there is a trajectory, and overall it's been pretty positive.

That matters more to me than whether she is No. 99, No. 102 or No. 108 next Monday. The concern is what happens when she returns. Falling outside the Top 100 creates practical problems. Raducanu may no longer receive automatic entry into some events, and if her ranking remains around this level when the Australian Open entry list is determined in December, qualifying could become a possibility.

Wild cards will probably remain available to her at many tournaments because she is Emma Raducanu. That is another privilege worth acknowledging. But the objective for 2027 should probably have very little to do with rushing to repair a ranking. It should be staying on a tennis court.

If that means beginning the year in qualifying somewhere, qualify. If it means playing smaller events, play them. Even if it means returning slowly enough that the Australian Open becomes less important than being healthy in March, so be it. Raducanu has spent too much of her career trying to get back somewhere. Back to the Top 100. Back to being seeded. Back to the player from New York. At some point, perhaps the healthier project is simply finding out what player she can become from here.

Emma Raducanu falling outside the Top 100 would make an excellent headline. It sounds dramatic, and everybody will click. A Former US Open champion tumbles outside the world's best 100. Five years removed from New York, another low. All technically true. Also slightly misleading.

She did not spend the summer losing herself out of the Top 100. She spent it unable to play. Before the stress fracture, she was No. 31 and had just reached a WTA 500 final. Earlier in the year, she had climbed to No. 23, her highest ranking since 2022.

Of course, there are still criticisms to make of the career. There should be. The coaching instability has been excessive. The consistency has never matched the talent. Five years after winning the US Open, having one career title is a strange record. Most importantly, she has not yet shown that her body can withstand the uninterrupted demands of a full season.

But this particular fall feels different. For once, Raducanu had begun doing many of the things people had been asking her to do. She was playing regularly and was reaching finals. She was beginning to look less like the girl trying to recreate one impossible fortnight and more like a professional tennis player building a sustainable career.

Then she got hurt. Again. Perhaps that is the saddest part of the Raducanu story so far. Every time the conversation begins moving away from 2021, something seems to drag it back. Yet, she is still only 23. The story still has time to become considerably less complicated.

Right now, the ranking says No. 100. Soon it may say something worse. For once, though, that number probably tells us less about Emma Raducanu than it appears to.

articles.title: Nadal: "Desde que me retiré, solo había jugado cuatro veces al tenis"
articles.standfirst: El ex tenista español atendió a los medios en la previa del 'Rafa Nadal Academy Slam'
articles.summary: El ex tenista español atendió a los medios en la previa del 'Rafa Nadal Academy Slam'
articles.body: Rafa Nadal vuelve a las pistas de tenis. Sí, lo hace en el slam que él mismo organiza para conmemorar 10 años de su academia en Manacor. Un evento, que desde que se anunció, ha revolucionado el mundo del tenis. Horas antes de que arranque, Nadal atiende a los medios junto al resto de participantes: Murray, Moyá, Ferrer, Gasquet, Thiem, Fognini y Safin. Una rueda de prensa que comenzó con el agradecimiento de Rafa a todos los asistentes: "En primer lugar quiero darle las gracias al resto de jugadores que han venido a participar en este torneo. Es un día muy especial para la academia y personalmente solo os puedo dar las gracias. Sabemos que puede ser un día difícil de lluvia, pero lo vamos a intentar para que sea una jornada inolvidable". La importancia para Rafa de los resultados durante su carrera: "No era más feliz siendo el número uno o el dos. Había cosas más importantes, aunque obviamente quieres ser el mejor. Siempre intenté dar mi mejor versión, superándome, sin importar tanto el ranking final". 683 días de su último partido como profesional, qué tanto por ciento del Rafa competidor veremos hoy: "El 0% del Rafa Nadal competidor sale hoy. Estoy en otra etapa. He disfrutado estas dos semanas de tocar la bola, había jugado muy poco antes, desde que me retiré, unas cuatro veces, media hora, poco más. Hoy la competición es lo de menos, es una fiesta de la academia. No tengo ninguna ambición competitiva". El futuro de la academia: "Ojalá lo pudiera saber. Uno nuca sabe qué va a ocurrir en el futuro. Debemos estar muy atentos para adaptarnos a los nuevos tiempos y poder expandirnos aún más en el mundo. Creo que estamos en un momento clave para evolucionar y en ello vamos a trabajar". La salud mental durante su carrera y un futuro como entrenador: "He tenido un buen equilibrio mental en mi carrera. El dolor diario afectaba al carácter, es cierto. Llevo desde que me retiré con poco dolor diario. Es cierto que me tuve que poner una prótesis en la mano. El futuro dirá, creo que en algún momento jugaré alguna exhibición. Da pereza el proceso, pero creo que es algo que debo testar. Nunca digas nunca (sobre ser entrenador). Estoy abierto a ayudar a quien me lo pida, pero tengo dos niños pequeños y muchas cosas que no me permitirían serlo". Las derrotas sobre su carrera y un consejo a los más jóvenes: Los momentos más duros son las lesiones, no las derrotas. Todos sabemos a lo que jugamos. El tenis es un deporte de perdedores, porque cada semana gana uno y perdemos el resto, no hay empates. La derrota además es parte del camino y te ayuda a crecer". El proceso de preparación para este partido y la ausencia de Federer: "No ha sido tan bonito como pueda parecer. Cuesta adaptarse respecto a lo que uno estaba habituado. Federer ha venido durante este verano, hubiera sido un placer contar con él pero le era imposible. Él siempre ha apoyado a la academia, estuvo en la inauguración y es fantástico ese apoyo".

articles.title: Bucsa es la víctima de Xinran Sun, la nueva niña prodigio del tenis
articles.standfirst: La china, de tan sólo 16 años, pasa a la tercera ronda del WTA 1000 de Pekín
articles.summary: La china, de tan sólo 16 años, pasa a la tercera ronda del WTA 1000 de Pekín
articles.body: China, el gigante asiático, se ilusiona con Xinran Sun. A sus 16 años, tras recibir una invitación del WTA 1000 de Pekín para hacer su debut en el circuito profesional, se ha clasificado este sábado para la tercera ronda del torneo de la capital tras derrotar a Cristina Bucsa, por 6-4 y 7-5. La tenista de Torrelavega estuvo exenta de la ronda inicial por su condición de vigésimo séptima cabeza de serie. Su, que había eliminado en el debut a Eva Lys (la alemana tuvo que retirarse por lesión tras perder el primer set), tocó la cima en categoría júnior el pasado mes de junio al convertirse en la tercera número 1 mundial de su país. Antes se había impuesto en dos ediciones consecutivas de la Orange Bowl. Perdió las finales de Roland Garros y Wimbledon contra rivales mayores que ella como Alisa Oktiabreva y Anna Pushkareva. Y se desquitó recientemente de Pushkareva con la corona del US Open, tras un tanteo de 6-4, 4-6 y 6-0. La nueva niña prodigio siempre ha confesado su admiración por Novak Djokovic y su compatriota Na Li. China, huérfana de una gran campeona desde que Li colgó la raqueta, sueña con el futuro esplendoroso de Xinran. Natural de Shenzhen, emigró a Serbia a los 10 años. Sus entrenadores son los locales Goran Zivotic y Goran Krivokuca. Sun se las verá en la tercera ronda con Coco Gauff, doble campeona de Grand Slam y cuarta raqueta del circuito femenino. De momento, ha escalado del puesto 582 al 418. La eliminación de Bucsa deja sin españolas el cuadro individual de Pekín. Cristina sigue viva en dobles al lado de Melichar-Martinez.

articles.title: World No 1 Sinner withdraws from Shanghai Masters as knee injury lingers
articles.summary: Italy’s Jannik Sinner has not played since Wimbledon win in July, missing US Open and ongoing ATP 500 event in Beijing.
articles.body:
World number ‌one Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from next ⁠week’s Shanghai ⁠Masters tennis tournament as he continues his recovery from a knee injury that has sidelined him since winning ⁠the Wimbledon men’s singles title in July.

The Italian, 25, has not played since his triumph at the All England ⁠Club, missing the North American hardcourt swing, including the US Open, and the ongoing ATP 500 event in Beijing.

“Unfortunately, I won’t be able to play at the ‌Rolex Shanghai Masters this year as I had hoped,” Sinner wrote on Instagram on Saturday.

“I always enjoy playing in front of the Shanghai fans and I’m very sorry that I won’t be able to do so next week.”

The Masters 1000 event runs from Wednesday to October 18 and features a ⁠strong field, led by four-time champion Novak Djokovic along with Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvedev, Ben Shelton, Felix Auger-Aliassime and defending ⁠champion Valentin Vacherot.

Sinner won the Shanghai title in 2024, defeating Djokovic in ⁠the final.

Sinner’s absence could boost Zverev’s ⁠push to finish the season as the world number one. The German, who was the French Open and US Open champion this year, has emerged as ‌the Italian’s closest challenger.

Zverev can move to the top of the rankings for the first time if he ‌wins ‌both the China Open in Beijing and the Shanghai Masters.

articles.title: Elena Rybakina suffers shock defeat to world No 118 Alina Charaeva after US Open triumph
articles.summary: Rybakina suffers sensational loss in China; Coco Gauff returned to action with a win but Harriet Dart was knocked out; Carlos Alcaraz secured a spot in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open; watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Rybakina reached the top of the world rankings after winning the US Open last month - her second Grand Slam title of 2026 - but was brought crashing back down to earth with a 6-3 4-6 3-6 defeat to Alina Charaeva at the China Open on Saturday afternoon.

Armenia's Charaeva had never faced a top-20 player before this match, but stunned the top seed to set up a round-of-32 clash with Britain's Sonay Kartal.

"I don't have words," said Charaeva after the victory of her life.

"This is incredible. Of course Elena is an amazing player who is doing really good this season winning two Grand Slams.

"For me it's just a dream come true. I just tried to stay hard mentally and keep believing I could turn around the game to my side.

Alcaraz battles to book quarter-finals spot at Japan Open

Carlos Alcaraz battled through a gripping first-set tie-break to book a spot in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open with a 7-6 (8-6) 6-1 victory over Matteo Arnaldi.

The Spaniard will face world No 46 Denis Shapovalov in the last eight, after the Canadian defeated Alejandro Tabilo 7-5 3-6 6-4 in Tokyo.

After going 2-5 down in the tie-break, Alcaraz saved four set points before flipping the decider on its head and go 1-0 up.

The world No 3 found another gear in the second set, breaking Arnaldi twice to seal victory.

"I just tried to stay there, point after point," Alcaraz said.

"I changed how I played until that moment and it worked out. I'm just happy I got that first set. Matteo was playing great."

Elsewhere in Tokyo, Jiri Lehecka came from behind to secure a 5-7 6-4 6-4 win against Ugo Humbert and set up a quarter-final clash against Adolfo Daniel Vallejo Alvarez , who knocked out Italian Matteo Berrettini.

At the China Open, US Open champion Alexander Zverev set up a blockbuster quarter-final tie against Novak Djokovic after the German No 1 seed brushed past wildcard Juncheng Shang 6-0 6-3.

After suffering a second-round defeat at the US Open, Alex de Minaur has returned to winning ways, with the Australian overcoming France's Quentin Halys in three sets on Saturday to set up a quarter-final clash with Andrey Rublev.

A spot in the semi-finals isn't the only thing up for grabs in this match, with both De Minaur and Rublev battling for Race to Turin points, as both look to secure one of the final spots at this year's ATP Finals.

Rublev booked his spot in the quarters after he bounced back from a second-set comeback from Roman Safiullin to win 6-2 3-6 6-4.

Daniil Medvedev sealed a straight-sets win over Jan-Lennard Struff , and will face the winner of Francisco Cerundolo's tie against Jakub Mensik .

Gauff returns with a win, Dart knocked out

Following her semi-final defeat to Rybakina at the US Open, Coco Gauff returned from a three-week break and booked her spot in the third round at the China Open, with a 7-6(7-4) 4-6 6-2 win over world No 66 Camila Osorio .

The two-time Grand Slam champion outlasted the Colombian in a first-set tie-break, before being broken at 4-5 to concede the following set.

Osorio battled hard in the final exchange, saving two match points, but Gauff would see out the victory and set up a tie against China's Xinran Sun in the next round.

Britain's Harriet Dart started strongly in her match against 10th seed Iva Jovic , taking the opening set.

However, she keep couldn't her foot on the accelerator, losing the next two sets in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

After being knocked out in the last 16 at the US Open, Iga Swiatek returned to action on Saturday and converted five break points to earn a dominant 6-2 6-3 win against China's Xinyu Gao .

Elsewhere, Elina Svitolina was forced to battle back from going a set down against Czech Katerina Siniakova , as she secured her spot in the next round with a 1-6 6-4 6-2 victory.

articles.title: Zverev gana en 55 minutos como un nº1 y amenaza el reinado de Djokovic en Pekín
articles.standfirst: El alemán arroya al chino Shang con rosco incluido y se cruza con Djokovic en su camino al número 1
articles.summary: El alemán arroya al chino Shang con rosco incluido y se cruza con Djokovic en su camino al número 1
articles.body: Alexander Zverev ha sacado el rodillo a pasear en Pekín. El público del National Tennis Center ha visto en un abrir y cerrar de ojos cómo el alemán se ha deshecho del jugador chino Shang Juncheng (250 del mundo) por 6-0 y 6-3 en 55 minutos de encuentro. Zverev, el mayor ganador de la actual campaña con 58 victorias, apenas dejó oportunidades sobre la central de la capital china. Un rosco (6-0) en tan solo 22 minutos abría el partido de forma muy favorable para el de Hamburgo. Tan solo cedió siete puntos en toda la manga. En el segundo set, Shang consiguió convertir tres juegos al servicio pero nunca llegó a intimidar al campeón de dos de los últimos tres grandes. Una victoria que acerca un poco más al alemán a la cima del ranking ATP. Shang, jugador zurdo, se suma a la lista de víctimas. El balance de Sascha ante jugadores de esta condición es de 48-1 desde Roland Garros 2023. La distancia entre las dos primeras raquetas mundiales se reduce a 1.280 puntos. Con la baja del de San Cándido del Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18 de octubre) por problemas en la rodilla derecha, restará 50 puntos más por la tercera ronda del TMS asiático. Sascha tendrá todavía más a tiro el trono del circuito masculino ya que solo está encargado de defender 1.080 puntos en lo que resta de temporada por los 3.000 del italiano. Alexander Zverev batallará ante Novak Djokovic por un puesto en las semifinales del torneo. "Estoy emocionado por el partido. Esta es seguramente una de sus pistas favoritas en su carrera, él nunca ha perdido aquí", declaraba el teutón tras el partido. El serbio firma un historial impecable sobre las pistas de Pekín. Ha salido victorioso en los 31 encuentros que ha disputado, manteniendo la segunda mejor racha ganadora inicial en un certamen junto a Rafa Nadal en Roland Garros (31). Solo es superado por las 33 de Monica Seles en el Australian Open.

articles.summary: Jannik Sinner announced his withdrawal from the China Open due to a knee injury and confirmed on Saturday he would also skip next week's Rolex Shanghai Masters; watch ATP Japan Open and WTA/ATP China Open this week live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
On Friday, the Italian announced he would not defend his title at the China Open, having previously skipped the US Open due to the injury.

Sinner has now not played since he defended his Wimbledon title against Alexander Zverev in July.

After revealing he was "not ready to compete" in Beijing last week, Sinner expressed his disappointment at having to now pull out of the Shanghai Masters, which commences on October 7 and is live on Sky Sports .

"I always enjoy playing in front of the Shanghai fans and I'm very sorry that I won't be able to do so next week," Sinner wrote on Instagram.

"Thank you for all your support. I'm looking forward to seeing you again next year!"

The world No 1 said last week that the injury was still not quite right.

Zverev, meanwhile, has pulled ahead of Sinner in the Race to Turin Ranking, with the German now 800 points clear of the five-time Grand Slam champion.

The injury means Sinner's hopes of finishing the 2026 season as the year-end No 1 have taken a big hit.

Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton, who all currently occupy spots in the top eight of the Race to Turin Rankings, are set to feature at the Shanghai Masters.

articles.title: China Open: Sonay Kartal wins as Alexander Zverev sets up Novak Djokovic clash
articles.summary: Great Britain's Sonay Kartal reaches last-32 at the China Open as Alexander Zverev sets up a quarter-final clash against Novak Djokovic in Beijing.
articles.body:
Great Britain's Sonay Kartal maintained her winning return to the WTA Tour with an impressive straight-set victory over home hope Wang Xinyu at the China Open.

Kartal, 24, produced a dominant display to see off the Chinese 31st seed Wang 6-3 6-2 in only her second tour match after six months out with a back injury.

She was expected to face newly crowned world number one Elena Rybakina in the last 32, but the top seed from Kazakhstan fell to a shock three-set defeat by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Elsewhere, men's top seed Alexander Zverev cruised past China's Juncheng Shang 6-0 6-3 to book a quarter-final against Novak Djokovic.

GB's Kartal wins on WTA return after six months out

'Just a number' - Rybakina's rise to world number one

Sabalenka 'trying hard to be easier on myself'

Kartal made the quarter-finals in Beijing in 2025 but had slipped down to 129 in the world after missing the majority of this season, including the past three Grand Slam tournaments.

She retired injured from a last-16 clash against Rybakina at Indian Wells in March and did not return to competitive action until last month's Billie Jean King Cup Finals.

Yet after earning a comfortable win over Spain's Andrea Lazaro Garcia on her return to tour duty at the China Open, Kartal followed that up with a clinical performance in beating Wang.

She produced 12 winners and made just 11 unforced errors, compared to her opponent's 24, converting five of her 14 break points with some impressive groundstrokes.

"I am super happy to play here and I think that shows in my tennis," Kartal said in her on-court interview, as she recalled her run to last year's quarter-final.

"I've had a long time out but I am happy to make a return to this event - I am looking to equal or hopefully do better this year."

To do that, Kartal would have been preparing herself to face Rybakina, but the US Open champion was well below her best in a disappointing 6-3 4-6 3-6 defeat by unseeded Charaeva, who had never before faced a top 20 player on the WTA Tour.

Meanwhile, Kartal's British team-mate Harriet Dart produced an encouraging display in a three-set defeat by American 10th seed Iva Jovic.

The 30-year-old British qualifier looked capable of causing an upset after claiming three breaks of serve in the opening set to charge into an early lead before eventually losing out 2-6 6-3 6-3 to the rising 18-year-old.

Zverev into last eight as Sinner puts off comeback

Zverev maintained his fine form in a season that has seen the German win his first two Grand Slam titles - the French Open and US Open - to set up a tantalising clash with Djokovic on Sunday.

Djokovic, 39, has won the China Open six times and has never lost a match at the event in Beijing, but Zverev knows that he will rise to number one in the world for the first time in his career should he win the China Open and Shanghai Masters, which starts on Wednesday (7 October).

The 29-year-old German's chances were boosted on Saturday when current world number one Jannik Sinner announced his decision to withdraw from the Shanghai Masters.

Italian Sinner is recovering from a knee injury and has not played since beating Zverev in the final of Wimbledon in July.

Sinner took the number one spot in April from Spain's Carlos Alcaraz, who returned from four months out with a wrist injury at the US Open in September.

World number three Alcaraz made it through to the quarter-finals of the Japan Open in Tokyo in Saturday, saving four set points in the opener against Italian Matteo Arnaldi before powering back to win 7-6 (8-6) 6-1.

Alcaraz will next play Canadian Denis Shapovalov following his 7-5 3-6 6-4 victory over Chile's Alejandro Tabilo.

articles.title: Nadal vuelve a ganar en un día "inolvidable"
articles.standfirst: MARCA es testigo de la vuelta del español a las pistas de tenis en el slam de su academia
articles.summary: MARCA es testigo de la vuelta del español a las pistas de tenis en el slam de su academia
articles.body: Manacor fue testigo de un hecho histórico: la vuelta de Rafa Nadal a las pistas de tenis y además, con victoria del equipo capitaneado por él. Fue en Manacor, en un día muy especial para su academia que cumplía 10 años. Que mejor manera que hacerlo con un torneo, el 'Rafa Nadal Academy Slam', que reunió a Murray, Moyá, Ferrer, Gasquet, Thiem, Fognini y Safin, junto al propio Rafa. Una jornada en la que se celebraba el éxito de un modelo, el de la academia de tenis, que es parte del legado que Rafa deja. Oportunidad perfecta, la de su décimo aniversario, para que Nadal volviera al lugar en el que tanto nos hizo disfrutar. El tiempo amenazaba con interrumpir una tarde para el recuerdo... pero no se atrevió. Durante la mañana, todos los integrantes del 'Rafa Nadal Academy Slam' asistieron a la sala de medios. Pero no lo hicieron para una rueda de prensa al uso, lo hicieron para algo mucho más divertido y desenfadado. Fue más bien una excusa para recordar, en público, anécdotas y momento vividos dentro y fuera de las pistas de tenis. "Hoy no vais a ver a un Rafa competitivo, lo de hoy es para disfrutar", aseguró Nadal mientras el resto de los tenistas se miraban cómplices... pensando que el mejor tenista español de la historia no sabe coger una raqueta de tenis sin apretar el acelerador. 683 días habían pasado desde el último partido de Rafa como profesional. Poco menos de dos año en los que tan sólo jugó al tenis cuatro veces... pero hay cosas que no se olvidan, cosas que no se pierden. Zidane no es el que era, obviamente, pero denle un balón de fútbol e inconscientemente empezarán a escuchar música clásica en su cabeza mientras ven al francés de nuevo en el verde. Hagan lo mismo, en este caso con uno de baloncesto, con Lebron James. Pueden imaginar lo que fue volver a ver a Rafa, con su raqueta, en su tierra'. Seis partidos, de dobles, a super 'tie-breaks' y cada victoria: un punto. El ‘Team Rafa’ (Nadal, Moyá, Ferrer y Gasquet) vs. el ‘Team Murray’ (Andy, Thiem, Fognini y Safin). Hubo de todo. Victorias por la mínima, 10-0, risas, puntazos, 'aces' de Nadal... Una fiesta del tenis que hizo disfrutar a los amantes de la raqueta y que... retrató las palabras de Rafa esa misma mañana. Menos mal que no iba a competir. Es su ADN, el mismo que le ha llevado a lo más alto y que le sigue empujando a apretar cada bola con todo lo que tiene. La calidad de Moyá también merece un reconocimiento. Al igual que al de Ferrer, Murray... todos regalaron puntos impresionantes y muchas bromas. Es cierto que cuando corría la bola querían dejar su sello, pero entre puntos (especialmente Safin), hicieron reír al público. Fue una tarde que el mundo del tenis tardará en olvidar. 10 años de academia, la vuelta de Rafa a los 'ruedos', Manacor, amigos de profesión, victoria... muchos ingredientes y muy buenos. Que buena 'excusa', la del éxito del Rafa Nadal Academy Slam, para que no haga falta esperar al vigésimo aniversario de la academia para volverlo a vivir. Sienta un gran precedente, que ojalá perdure.
